rubrics.name: STAAR ECR — Extended Constructed Response
rubrics.subject: RLA
rubrics.blurb: Official-style 5-point ECR: Organization & Development (0–3) plus Conventions (0–2). If development is 0, conventions must be 0.
rubrics.studentTitle: How I’ll score my extended response

levels.teacher: No response, too limited to score, or off the prompt. Controlling idea is missing.
levels.student: I did not answer the prompt, or my idea is not clear.

levels.teacher: Weak development. Thin or unclear controlling idea, little relevant evidence, organization is hard to follow.
levels.student: I started an idea but did not explain it with enough text evidence.

levels.teacher: Partial development. Controlling idea is present. Some relevant evidence and a basic structure.
levels.student: I stated an idea and used some evidence, but a reader still has questions.

levels.teacher: Fully developed. Clear controlling idea, relevant text evidence, purposeful organization, and explanation that holds together.
levels.student: I stated a clear idea, used strong evidence from the text, and explained how it all fits.

levels.teacher: Little command of grade-level conventions, or auto-zero because development scored 0. Errors impede meaning.
levels.student: Mistakes make my writing hard to read — or I did not develop an idea, so conventions cannot count.

levels.teacher: Partial command. Errors are noticeable and sometimes get in the way, but a reader can still follow.
levels.student: I have some spelling, capital, or sentence mistakes, but a reader can still follow me.

levels.teacher: Consistent command of grade-level conventions. Errors are minor and do not impede meaning.
levels.student: My sentences, spelling, and punctuation are mostly correct so my ideas are easy to read.

rubrics.name: STAAR SCR — Reading (2-point)
rubrics.subject: RLA
rubrics.blurb: Short constructed response to a reading question. Score 0–2 for completeness, accuracy, and text evidence.
rubrics.studentTitle: How I’ll score my short reading response

levels.teacher: Incorrect, blank, or no meaningful connection to the text or question.
levels.student: I did not answer the question, or my answer does not match the text.

levels.teacher: Partial. Some accuracy but missing evidence, incomplete explanation, or only part of the question addressed.
levels.student: I started to answer but missed evidence or only answered part of the question.

levels.teacher: Complete and accurate. Addresses the question and uses relevant text evidence.
levels.student: I answered the question and backed it up with evidence from the text.

rubrics.name: STAAR SCR — Writing (1-point)
rubrics.subject: RLA
rubrics.blurb: Short writing revision or composition task. Score 0 or 1 for a complete, acceptable response.
rubrics.studentTitle: How I’ll score my short writing task

levels.teacher: Incorrect, too limited, off-task, or blank.
levels.student: I did not complete the writing task.

levels.teacher: Addresses the task with a sufficient, acceptable response.
levels.student: I completed the writing task and my answer makes sense.

rubrics.name: RACE constructed response
rubrics.subject: RLA
rubrics.blurb: Classroom RACE checklist (Restate, Answer, Cite, Explain). Use for daily practice before STAAR ECR/SCR.

levels.label: No
levels.teacher: Question is not restated.
levels.student: I did not restate the question.

levels.label: Yes
levels.teacher: Opening restates the question in the student’s own words.
levels.student: I restated the question in my first sentence.

levels.label: No
levels.teacher: No clear answer to the prompt.
levels.student: I did not give a clear answer.

levels.label: Yes
levels.teacher: A direct, on-prompt answer is stated.
levels.student: I answered the question clearly.

levels.label: No
levels.teacher: No relevant evidence.
levels.student: I did not use words from the text.

levels.label: Yes
levels.teacher: Relevant evidence is cited.
levels.student: I used evidence from the text.

levels.label: No
levels.teacher: Evidence is dropped in without explanation.
levels.student: I did not explain my evidence.

levels.label: Yes
levels.teacher: Student explains how the evidence supports the answer.
levels.student: I explained how the evidence proves my answer.

rubrics.name: Classroom 4-level product rubric
rubrics.subject: Any
rubrics.blurb: Blank 4-level skeleton you can duplicate and rename for any TEKS product: beginning, developing, proficient, distinguished.

levels.label: Beginning
levels.teacher: Little evidence of the skill.
levels.student: I am just getting started on this skill.

levels.label: Developing
levels.teacher: Partial evidence; important pieces missing.
levels.student: I showed some of the skill but not all of it.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.teacher: Meets the standard with solid evidence.
levels.student: I met the goal for this skill.

levels.label: Distinguished
levels.teacher: Exceeds with precise, thorough evidence.
levels.student: I went beyond the goal with clear, strong work.

levels.label: Beginning
levels.teacher: Hard to follow; unfinished.
levels.student: My work is unfinished or hard to follow.

levels.label: Developing
levels.teacher: Partly organized; some conventions issues.
levels.student: My work is partly organized.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.teacher: Clear, complete, readable.
levels.student: My work is clear and complete.

levels.label: Distinguished
levels.teacher: Polished and easy for an audience to use.
levels.student: My work is polished and easy for others to use.
